News.title: Another high street coffee chain hires BOUNCERS to guard their food & drink amid shoplifting epidemic
News.content:
ANOTHER high street coffee chain is employing bouncers to guard their food and drink amid a shoplifting epidemic.

Pret A Manger has become the latest high street chain forced to bring in security officers, following in the footsteps of Costa, Greggs and McDonald’s.





Pictures captured in West Hampstead, London, show a security worker on high alert as he stands at the entrance to one of the coffee chain’s stores.

The guard has seemingly been brought in to protect the staff and products in the sandwich shop.

It comes after a wave of shoplifting thefts ravaged the British high street with food and drink lifted from shelves in broad daylight by brazen thieves.

Pret A Manger is understood to employ third party security in locations where it is felt appropriate by the company.

Pret said it regularly reviewed the use of security officers and offered additional support when and where it was needed.

Earlier this year Costa – Britain’s biggest coffee chain – confirmed it had hired “additional support” to ensure stores are safe for its staff and customers.

It followed on the heels of a slew of thefts at Greggs, revealed by The Sun last year, thought to be costing the bakery millions of pounds a year.

Elsewhere, staff at M&S were issued with body-worn cameras amid the snowballing shoplifting crisis.



Separate measures were introduced at Sainsbury’s with the chain of stores using checkout cameras that records would-be thieves who fail to scan items before playing the footage back to them.

And, in 2024 it was revealed that staff members in London based Pret A Manger stores were issued with body-worn cameras.

Video footage from the cameras, which would only be turned on under specific circumstances, would be shared with Pret’s security team.



The personal cameras were set to be trialled at six of the sandwich shop’s locations in the capital.

The introduction of the technology came as companies reported increasing cases of shoplifting and aggressive behaviour towards staff.

Now, the chain appears to have hired guards to patrol some of its stores in the capital in a further bid to beef up their security.

Government figures revealed there were 519,381 shop thefts across England and Wales in the year to September 2025, up five per cent from 492,660 in 2024.

However, some chains have stopped reporting incidents, with just 46,000 prosecutions last year.



Lucy Whing of the British Retail Consortium, previously told The Sun: “Retailers have invested over £5billion in the last five years to tackle theft and crime.

“Ultimately such theft is not a victimless crime, pushing up the price for honest shoppers.”

In the wake of the rise in retail related crime stores are now splashing cash on security cameras, personnel, CCTV and body-worn cameras, the British Retail Consortium said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Pret spokesperson told The Sun: “For several years Pret has used security personnel in some of its shops to ensure the safety and wellbeing of team members and customers.

“We regularly review this, introducing additional support where it may be appropriate.”

News.title: Mum made daughter ‘keep lookout as she spiked son’s smoothie with cocktail of drugs to cash in on £50k life insurance’
News.content:
A MUM made her daughter “keep lookout” while she laced her son’s fruit smoothie with a lethal cocktail of drugs for an insurance pay out, a jury has heard.

Maree Mavis Crabtree is alleged to have secretly blended a deadly dose of painkillers into a drink she then gave to her son Jonathan, 26, before leaving him to die in his bedroom.





The 59-year-old woman is standing trial at Brisbane Supreme Court over the alleged killing at the Australian family home near the Gold Coast in July 2017.

Jonathan’s sister Tara Crabtree – who has been granted immunity from prosecution – told the jury on Friday she helped her mother by keeping lookout while the smoothie was prepared.

“She cut up fruit and put it in the blender to blend it…watermelon, pretty sure mango, pineapple are the main ones I remember,” Tara shared in a pre-recorded video.

Tara, who was just one year younger than Jonathan, said her mother then used a hammer to crush a collection of pills on a chopping board before adding the powder into the smoothie.

Crabtree also allegedly added six bottles of liquid oxycodone opiate painkiller.

Tara said: “She asked me to keep lookout for my brother. He came out and she gave it to him.”

When asked why Crabtree put drugs in her brother’s smoothie, Tara said her mum thought he was a “violent and horrible” person to live with.

“We would have more peace and live a better life without him, that’s what she said,” Tara said.



She then told the jury how her mum told her not to offer help to her brother after she heard him struggling and making noises in his room.

Tara also said her mum told her not say anything to police when they arrived.

“He committed suicide, that’s what she told me to say,” Tara said.

Earlier, jurors heard emergency services were called on the morning of July 19 after Crabtree reported her son was not breathing.

But Crown prosecutor Caroline Marco said she allegedly refused to perform CPR when urged by the triple-0 operator.



“She had a bad back and that she could not stay in the room with him ‘as she thought he was then dead’,” Ms Marco told the court.

When paramedics arrived at the home about 9.55am they found Jonathan lying on his bed with his legs hanging to the floor and a Spider-Man backpack nearby.

The jury heard he was already showing “obvious signs that he had been dead for hours.”



Prosecutors allege the fatal drink was disguised with fruit to mask the smell of the drugs.

Prosecutors claim Crabtree later made a dishonest claim for a death benefit from Jonathan’s superannuation fund.

At the time of his death, Jonathan shared ownership of the Maudsland home with his sister, while their mother lived there but was not listed on the title.

Ms Marco said the household was often tense and that Jonathan had been a “troubled young man” who abused drugs.

He had previously been charged with robbing a chemist and suffered permanent injuries in a serious car crash in 2015 that left him needing physical care.



The court heard Crabtree had told people her son was “difficult and abusive”.

“She told Tara that his involvement in the robbery had put their family’s finances in jeopardy, which was the reason why she needed to kill him,” Ms Marco said.

Investigators later found numerous bottles of liquid oxycodone inside the house and a smoothie blender that tested positive for drugs.

But Crabtree’s defence team says the case hinges entirely on whether jurors believe her daughter’s version of events.

Barrister Angus Edwards told the court Tara had admitted lying to police and only accused her mother more than two years after Jonathan’s death.



“That is the real issue in this trial. Do you believe Tara Crabtree’s story?” he said.

He suggested Jonathan – described as a “violent, suicidal, drug addict” – could have taken the drugs himself.

“Somehow those drugs got into him,” Mr Edwards said.

“There is of course the possibility that Jonathan Crabtree, deliberately or accidentally, had an overdose of drugs to which he had access.”

Mr Edwards also questioned Tara’s motives for speaking out.



“What are her motives when she came out with this story about her mother? Is something sinister going on here?” he asked.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Crabtree has denied murdering her son and attempting to murder her him months earlier.

She also denies attempting to fraudulently claim more than £50,000 ($100,000) after his death.

News.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz ‘completely open’ for rest of 10-day ceasefire with US as Trump hails breakthrough
News.content:
STRAIT TO IT Iran declares Strait of Hormuz ‘completely open’ for rest of 10-day ceasefire with US as Trump hails breakthrough

IRAN has declared the Strait of Hormuz “completely open” for the rest of the temporary ceasefire.

Donald Trump celebrated the breakthrough on Truth Social, writing: “IRAN HAS JUST ANNOUNCED THAT THE STRAIT OF IRAN IS FULLY OPEN AND READY FOR FULL PASSAGE. THANK YOU!”



Iran’s foreign minister said the decision to open the shipping lane came after Israel agreed to stop blitzing Lebanon with a ten-day temporary ceasefire that started last night.



Seyed Abbas Aragchi said Iran would allow “all commercial vessels” through the Strait “for the remaining period of ceasefire”.

He added that vessels must stay “on the coordinated route as already announced”.

There is currently an American naval blockade stopping all ships that have visited Iranian ports from passing through the Strait.

Reopening the crucial oil choke point was a key plank in the two-week pause in fighting agreed between the US and Iran last Tuesday.

But the Iranians shut the Strait when Israel continued to pummel Lebanon, hammering the Hezbollah stronghold with huge attacks last week.

Iran previously claimed the Strait was open to all but its enemies, yet released a chilling map showing how tankers can weave through deadly sea mines in the waterway.

The US and Israel insisted that Lebanon was not covered by the ceasefire deal, but Iran was adamant that it should was.

And direct peace talks reportedly fell through between the US and Iran on Saturday when Tehran refused to stop enriching uranium.



Fresh hopes for peace have been kindled in recent days as Trump started to refer to the war in Iran in the past tense, hinting that more talks were coming soon.

Trump said he would not need to extend the two-week ceasefire, due to end on April 22, because the two sides are “very close” to a long-term peace deal.

The US president said last night that Iran had “agreed not to have a nuclear weapon”.

News.title: Woman arrested after girl, 7, drowned in golf course pond when she ‘escaped childminder through gap in park fence’
News.content:
POND TRAGEDY Woman arrested after girl, 7, drowned in golf course pond when she ‘escaped childminder through gap in park fence’

A WOMAN has been arrested after seven-year-old was found drowned on a golf course after she escaped her childminder through a gap in a park fence.

Nyla May Bradshaw was found dead in a pond in South Yorkshire last month after she was reported missing.





Her mum Hayley reportedly left the non-verbal autistic youngster with a specialist SEND childminder but just two hours later, she received a text saying Nyla had vanished.

South Yorkshire Police said today that a woman aged in her 30s has been arrested on suspicion of gross negligence manslaughter and child neglect.

She has been bailed pending further inquiries, the force said.

Detective Chief Inspector Gary Magnay said while initial inquiries had indicated the circumstances of Nyla’s death were not suspicious, police had “furthered (their) investigation into the events leading up to the incident”.

An inquest heard previously that on the day of the tragedy, she had been “taken out to a park in the Owston area of Doncaster”.

Nyla then passed through a hole in a fence and headed towards nearby woodland.

Coroner’s officer Jane McDonnell said a search was launched after the childminder raised the alarm with police and the youngster’s family.



She was later found unresponsive and face down in a pond on Owston Hall golf course in Doncaster.

Nyla was rushed to Doncaster Royal Infirmary but was tragically declared dead at 1.18pm.

Senior coroner Nicola Mundy adjourned the full inquest at Doncaster Coroner’s Court until December 8.

Family friend Charlotte Emma said the Ofsted-registered childminder had been told that Nyla was a “flight risk”.

She explained the youngster’s mum left Nyla with the new babysitter, who was “recommended over Facebook”, as her regular minder was fully booked.



Devastated parents Hayley and Kieran Bradshaw paid tribute to their daughter online.

In a heartbreaking post on her Facebook page, Nyla’s mother wrote: “It breaks my heart to write this, but today we lost our beautiful daughter Nyla May Bradshaw at just 7 years old.

“She was our whole world full of love, laughter, and the brightest smile that could light up any room.

“She brought so much joy into our lives and into the lives of everyone who knew her.”

Her dad Kieran Bradshaw described her as his “best friend” and an “amazing daughter”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He wrote on Facebook: “You were so loved Nyla you touched everyone’s heart that ever met you.

“I’ll never ever go a moment without you in my thoughts.”

News.title: Monster who murdered estranged wife will be back on the streets despite never revealing where her body is buried
News.content:
KILLER FREED Monster who murdered estranged wife will be back on the streets despite never revealing where her body is buried

A MONSTER who murdered his estranged wife and refused to reveal the location of her body has been granted parole.

Glyn Razzell is set to be freed after he was sentenced to a minimum of 16 years in prison for the death of mum-of-four Linda Razzell in 2002.





Linda vanished on her way to work in Swindon with cops eventually arresting and charging Razzell over her murder.

Now 66, the killer who has never admitted to the murder was convicted in 2003 after a lengthy trial – his estranged wife’s body was never found.

A search of Razzell’s borrowed car revealed a significant amount of blood in the boot which was matched to Linda.

Over an 18-month investigation, detectives spoke to 2,600 people, followed up more than 2,200 lines of enquiry and took 1,540 statements to jail Razzell.



He had been refused release on three separate occasions before and in 2021 became the first prisoner to be denied parole under Helen’s Law.

Named after Helen McCourt, who was murdered in 1988 and whose killer never revealed where her body was, Helen’s Law compels the Parole Board to consider a prisoner’s refusal to reveal the victim’s remains when assessing their suitability for release.

Despite previously being denied release, in January this year Razzell was granted parole as he went before the board yet again.

The murderer, who has been ruled as no longer a risk to the public, has been granted parole despite still refusing to reveal where his ex-wife’s body is.



Razzell and Linda, 41 at the time, had been going through a divorce prior to her death.

She was engaged to marry another man, Greg Worrall – who was in his 40s at the time – when the proceedings were finalised.

Greg has always maintained that Linda’s family believed Razzell should never be granted parole unless he showed remorse and gave up information on what happened to Linda’s body.

He said previously: “He’s never shown any remorse, which is a criteria for parole.

“If he wants to show remorse he’s got to stop saying he didn’t do it, turn up a body and allow her children a funeral.



“Jail has got to be a deterrent.”

The Parole Board said in a statement to the BBC: “We can confirm that a panel of the Parole Board has directed the release of Glyn Razzell following an oral hearing.

“Parole Board decisions are solely focused on what risk a prisoner could represent to the public if released and whether that risk is manageable in the community.



“A panel will carefully examine a huge range of evidence, including details of the original crime, and any evidence of behaviour change, as well as explore the harm done and impact the crime has had on the victims.

“Parole reviews are undertaken thoroughly and with extreme care. Protecting the public is our number one priority.”

Linda’s family have now told the BBC the parole board ruling “ripped up” Helen’s Law.

Greg, from Highworth, Wiltshire, said he and Linda planned to marry as soon as her divorce terms with Razzell were settled.

He said: “She was lovely. We both had bad relationships before and we agreed there was no love without respect.



“We’d written out our vows. It would be ‘love, honour and respect’.

“There’s no honour without respect and Razzell never respected women.”

Details of the Parole Board’s decision, published by the BBC, note the “continued cruelty” of Razzell’s refusal to reveal where Linda’s remains are.

Despite this it was concluded he was “no longer a risk to the public” with the Ministry of Justice now confirming it was looking at ways to contest the decision.

A spokesperson said: “Officials acting on behalf of the Secretary of State for Justice are examining if there are grounds to challenge the Parole Board’s decision through the reconsideration mechanism.”



Following the murderer’s conviction, Det Chief Insp Paul Granger, who led the team from Wiltshire Police that brought Razzell to justice, said: “I don’t think Razzell will tell us where the body is – and if he does it will not be for a long time.

“He is an evil, cold, calculated and intelligent man, but he made mistakes and that is how he ended up getting caught.”

A former investment manager at Zurich, Razzell showed no emotion as a guilty verdict was read out in court after six hours of jury deliberation.

During the trial, the court was told Linda had been due to receive the marital home in Pentylands Close, Highworth, and a £30,000 lump sum.

A month before Linda vanished Razzell had been acquitted of a charge of wounding after allegedly repeatedly hitting her head against a window in the home they shared.



Jurors were told Razzell had made throwaway comments to a friend about disposing of a body in quicksand near Cotswold Water Park and had discussed the financial benefits of killing his wife.

It was heard that he had started a new relationship with Rachel Smith, also from Wiltshire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2018, Razzell appeared on BBC miscarriage of justice programme Convicted in an effort to prove his innocence.

He refused to take a lie detector test when asked to by the programme team.

News.title: My manic neighbour tried to kill his nan before stabbing me 20 times, he screamed ‘die b****’ as I pleaded for my life
News.content:
EVIL NEXT DOOR My manic neighbour tried to kill his nan before stabbing me 20 times, he screamed ‘die b****’ as I pleaded for my life

HEARING a loud thud followed by banshee-like screaming in the flat above her, Kate King pressed record on her phone.

She wanted evidence of another frightening outburst from her nightmare neighbour, Matthew Macmillan. For months, he’d terrorised his nan, Carol, 82, in her home.





Minutes later, there was a knock at Kate’s door.

Opening it she was faced with knife-wielding Macmillan – his horrified nan staggering behind him.

Within seconds, crazed-Macmillan stabbed Carol before launching a terrifying attack on Kate, stabbing the helpless mother-of-two over 50 times.

Somehow, the 47-year-old, of Rhyl, Denbighshire, survived.

In January this year, Macmillan 38, pleaded guilty to two counts of attempted murder and was jailed for a minimum of 25 years with an extended five years to be served on licence.

Kate says: “It’s a miracle I survived that day.

“Thanks to the police officers, paramedics, air ambulance staff and Stoke Hospital.



“Without them, I wouldn’t be here today. I’m so grateful they saved my life.”

In July 2023, Kate moved into a new ground-floor flat with her Shichon dog, Bella.

She says: “Matthew lived with his nan in the flat above me. But from the moment I met him, I thought he was odd.

“Whenever he looked at me with his icy blue eyes, I felt like he was staring into my soul.”

Then one day, he walked by Kate’s garden.



She recalls: “He said ‘hello’ and I waved. He leaned over the fence and began moaning about not being able to find work. I encouraged him to keep trying.”

Only, what he said next sent shivers down Kate’s spine.

‘It’s difficult with a criminal record’, he told her.

Explained how he’d been to prison for eight months after getting into a fight on a night out.

Kate says: “I was horrified, yet didn’t let it show.



“From then on I became paranoid he was watching me through the bedroom window.

“As my dog, Bella would often bark at the spot.”

Then, six months later, Kate was startled awake at 3am one morning by an awful scream, followed by loud thuds.

She recalls: “I heard Matthew’s voice scream ‘Get me an ambulance!’

“I was tempted to phone the police, but he would suspect it was me and I didn’t want any trouble. So, I went back to sleep.”



A few days later, Kate bumped into Carol who apologised for the noise, claiming that Macmillan wasn’t well.

When Kate asked if he’d ever hurt her, she shook her head. Instead, insisted he was having an ‘episode’ and was having tests to find out what was wrong with him.

Kate says: “I worried for Carol. She was vulnerable and Matthew was a handful.”

Time passed and Kate heard him yelling upstairs again. Calling his nan an “old bitch’’.



Kate remembers: “I knocked on another neighbour’s door and we discussed his nightmare behaviour.

“I even told her I was worried Matthew would kill Carol one day.”

A few months on, in June 2025, Macmillan went on another rampage, slamming objects around his nan’s flat.

Then, soon after, Kate bumped into him outside her front door.

He told her: “I’m glad my nan has you, if anything happens to me, I know you’ll look after her.”



She had no idea what he meant. The following month, while in bed, Kate heard Macmillan shout: “Where’s my money?’’

She recalls: “Suddenly, I heard Carol scream like a banshee. I bolted up, terrified.

“Grabbing my phone, I pressed on video record, to start gathering evidence in case I ever needed it.”

Moments later, there was a knock at Kate’s door. Opening it, Carol was there as white as a sheet.

Kate says: “Seconds later, Matthew appeared and grabbed his nan, before dragging her into mine.



“Horror hit me as I spotted him clutching a 6inch knife.

“When he lunged at Carol, stabbing her over and over, I yelled ‘Matthew, stop!’”

“He then picked me up by my throat, before telling me to ‘Die, bitch’ Kate King ,

With that, Macmillan stormed towards Kate, plunging the knife into her forehead, before sinking his teeth into her left eyebrow.

Kate remembers: “Pain seared through me as he tore off my skin.

“He then picked me up by my throat, before telling me to ‘Die, bitch’.”



Bella, who was barking, rushed over to defend Kate and Macmillan threatened to ‘slice her open’ before yanking her up by her ears.

Then he swung her little body around Kate’s head and launched her across the living room.

She fell to a heap and wasn’t moving. Moments later, Macmillan pushed Carol outside into the hallway, before locking the front door.

Kate says: “It was then I thought I was going to die.

“As he lunged at me, I put my hands up to protect my face.



“He slashed at my body with the blade, before stabbing me over and over in my back.

“During the attack, he told me ‘I’m going to eat your skin’. My body throbbed in agony with every blow.”

Kate begged him to stop. But he told her “you won’t survive’’ and that he’d been planning to kill her since they’d met.

As Kate thrashed around, Macmillan shoved his hands into her mouth and tried to break her jaw.

She explains: “I felt my teeth break, before tasting blood.



“When he started stabbing me again, somehow I managed to grab the knife. As we wrestled, the blade snapped.”

But he produced another knife.

Kate recalls: “I heard the sound of glass shattering and the police announce themselves.

“But Matthew still had me pinned down, and they had to taser him three times before pulling him off.”

Paramedics arrived and stretchered Kate to an ambulance where she was then airlifted to Royal Stoke University Hospital.



She says: “Arriving, I was told my chances of survival were slim.

“So, in case I didn’t pull through, I agreed to a video declaration for evidence.”

Macmillan had stabbed Kate over 50 times during the 20-minute attack. She suffered five broken ribs, facial fractures, a broken shoulder.

Soon after, she was sedated and given a chest drain to treat a punctured lung and stitches to her face, back and left arm.

She says: “Hours later, my daughter and son arrived and told me my best friend had taken Bella to the vets.



“She had damage to her trachea.

“I was relieved she was alive.”

Meanwhile police informed Kate that Macmillan’s nan, Carol was stable and being treated for stab wounds in hospital.

Three days on, Kate was discharged and went to live with her children.

She says: “Losing five lower teeth left me embarrassed to eat and drink in front of them as I dribbled.



“I felt repulsive. Looking in the mirror seeing heavy scars line my face was a constant reminder of the attack.”

Four months on, Macmillan appeared at Mold Crown Court where Kate’s video capturing the start of her attack was shown.

The court heard how Macmillan had launched the attack after wrongly believing Kate and Carol had taken his £77,000 gambling winnings.

The judge jailed him for 25 years.

Kate says: “No amount of time will ever make up for the life-changing injuries and everlasting trauma.



“I live in constant pain. My face feels like acid is running down it.

“Even taking a shower triggers flashbacks.

“Taking me straight back to the attack, feeling him licking blood off my face and whispering at me to die, over and over.”

Now Kate is looking to start an organisation to provide trauma support for other victims of crime.

Starting with care packages for hospital stays during recovery.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She explains: “There’s a reason I’m still alive.

“And I’m determined to turn the worst experience of my life into something positive.”

News.title: Brit, 21, fights for life after quad bike crash in Greece as horrified girlfriend reveals hearing ‘huge bang’ from hotel
News.content:
HOLIDAY HORROR Brit, 21, fights for life after quad bike crash in Greece as horrified girlfriend reveals hearing ‘huge bang’ from hotel

A BRITISH Army reservist has been left fighting for his life in an induced coma after a horror quad bike crash in Greece.

Ethan Jones, 21, from Bradford, West Yorkshire, suffered devastating head injuries after the hired quad bike he was riding crashed into a bollard in Rhodes.





His girlfriend Olivia Alssopp, 20, heard the terrifying impact from their hotel before discovering the shocking scene moments later.

Olivia told The Sun: “I heard a massive skirt noise and a huge bang.”

When Ethan failed to answer repeated calls, she started panicking.

She said: “He normally answers his phone straight away. He’s not the type of person to not answer his phone.”

Fearing the worst, she rushed out onto the dark road – only to see Ethan lying on the floor next to a pool of blood.

Olivia said: “The quad bike was tipped over and he was against a big bollard. There was a pool of blood just bleeding from his head and his nose.”

With Ethan unresponsive and struggling to breathe, Olivia placed him in the recovery position and called for help.

Olivia continued: “I couldn’t even process what happened. I was just in shock. So much shock.”



The cause of the crash remains unclear.

An ambulance arrived within ten minutes – though Olivia said “it felt like forever” – but medics refused to take her with Ethan to the hospital.

In a frantic bid to stay close to him, she jumped in a taxi and rushed to the hospital, only to endure a 13-hour wait without being allowed to see him.

Olivia claimed staff were “really dismissive” and “no one was really helping”, handing her a letter in Greek explaining his condition.

She contacted the British Embassy, which arranged a translator to help.



Ethan has since been airlifted to Crete and placed into an induced coma, with Olivia now scrambling to join him.

The couple – together for three years – were due to fly back to the UK this Saturday after their week-long holiday.

Olivia’s dad, Daniel Allsopp, told The Sun: “I don’t know how we can hold it together. I’m just devastated.”

Describing Ethan, he said: “He’s just got a heart of gold. He protects Olivia. He wears his heart on his sleeve.”

The pair were not covered by insurance for quad bike accidents.



A GoFundMe page has now been set up by the family to help cover the cost of Ethan’s recovery and bring him back home to the UK.

Over £11,000 has already been raised – but the family faces a £25,000 target to cover the full cost of vital medical treatment.

More than 620 donations have been made so far with the highest donation being £500.

Olivia added: “We’re just hoping enough can be raised. I can’t even put into words how I feel because we don’t even know how much the expenses will be.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s just so much pressure on me because I’m out here by myself.”



The Sun has contacted the Foreign Office for comment.

News.title: Pilot faints in cockpit mid-air on early morning flight after ‘not sleeping the night before’
News.content:
MID-AIR PANIC Pilot faints in cockpit mid-air on early morning flight after ‘not sleeping the night before’

A PILOT has fainted in the cockpit mid-flight after reportedly not sleeping a wink the night before.

Emergency services raced onto the tarmac after receiving reports that the pilot, 57, had collapsed in the air while piloting a Tarom flight.



The pilot had reportedly started feeling unwell about 50minutes into the 6am flight from Bucharest’s Otopeni Airport.



The plane went on to land safely in Amsterdam, according to a report by the Civil Aviation Safety Investigation and Analysis Authority (AIAS) which did not mention the date.

Before the return flight back to Bucharest, the sickly pilot decided he wasn’t in a fit state to operate the controls and handed responsibility over to his co-pilot.

After almost an hour into the second flight, he reportedly started to feel ill again and fainted.

His shocked co-pilot raised the emergency alarm.

Medics were on standby to treat the pilot when the plane landed in Romanian capital.

All 87 passengers were safe and exited from the rear of the cabin.

The AIAS report found the ill pilot had gone to work having not slept the previous night.

He was reportedly affected by noise and the use of a solution against mosquitoes, Informat reported.



The pilot was reprimanded and is no longer allowed to fly on evening flights or flights longer than two hours.

He also won’t be scheduled again with the same co-pilot.

It comes after two pilots bark and meow at each other whilst an exasperated air controller tells the pair to “be professional”.

According to comments by the controller, the pair exchanged animal noises for over five minutes.



He reprimanded them: “You guys, uh, need to be professional pilots”.

The pilots took no heed, responding with a series of “meows” in quick succession.

In the bizarre audio clip, the other then chimed in with a high-pitched imitation of a dog barking.

“This is why you still fly an RJ (regional jet)”, the air controller quipped.

Pilots typically start out flying regional airlines at the beginning of their careers, though it is not clear if the pilots were flying passenger jets at the time of the exchange.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It was funny for the first five minutes”, he added, before the clip ends.

The pilot’s exchange was recorded near the fateful Ronald Reagan Washington National airport, the site of a horrific mid-air plane collision which left 67 people dead.

News.title: The heartwarming reason 1 Tube station has a different 'mind the gap' voice
News.content:
The heartwarming reason 1 Tube station has a different 'mind the gap' voice

One London Underground station has a "mind the gap" announcement which can't be heard anywhere else. One American man living in the UK explained the touching story behind it

View Image Regular users of the Tube will notice something unusual in the clip (stock image) (Image: PA)

An American living in the UK has revealed how a "strange experience" at a Tube station prompted him to discover a genuinely heartwarming tale. Russ, originally from Chicago but now based in the UK, frequently shares his perspectives on the contrasts between British and American culture on social media, where, under the name Red Bus Russ, he boasts more than 280,000 followers.

‌



He recently uploaded a video detailing a "strange experience" he encountered at an Underground station - and how it led him to uncover a genuinely moving story. Starting his video outside Embankment Station, he explained: "I just had the strangest experience at this Tube station.

‌



"So, I'm on my way to Covent Garden to do some filming [and] when I got off my train I heard this." The footage then switches to the platform, with the announcement "mind the gap" audible.

‌



To most people there would appear to be nothing remarkable about the clip - but regular Tube passengers will notice that the voice delivering the announcement differs from the one typically heard across the network. Russ went on: "I hadn't really noticed it before, but that's not the normal voice for the Underground. So I went to go look it up and it turns out that voice is there on purpose.

"That voice belongs to the late husband of a lady who would travel to Embankment Station and sit there for hours listening to the announcement again and again because that was the only way that she could hear his voice after he died. But in 2012 TFL updated their PA systems and they replaced the voice.

"Now, of course, the lady was very distraught by this, so she contacted TFL and asked 'could you please put my husband's voice back?'. TFL said 'well, we would, but we probably don't have the recording any more. It was recorded on tape decades ago and we're all digitised now'.

‌



"But after some digging they found the tape with her husband's voice. After that they reinstated her husband's voice to the announcement, and that's the one that you can hear at Embankment Station today. Very romantic of you TFL."

The voice is that of the late Oswald Laurence, whose "mind the gap" recording had echoed through the station for over four decades, until TFL moved to standardise announcements across the entire network in 2012, reports MyLondon.

Oswald died in 2007, and his widow, Margaret McCollum, regularly made her way to Embankment Station simply to hear her late husband's voice once more. Opening up to the BBC in 2013, she said: "If I had a journey that could possibly go via Embankment, I would do it that way... Since he died I would sit and wait for the next train until I heard his voice."

‌



But on November 1, 2012, she realised the announcement had been altered. "I was just stunned when Oswald wasn't there anymore," she said. "I inquired and I was told there was a new digital system and they could not get his voice on it."

She added: "I was horrified. I was completely, utterly devastated. That might sound ridiculous but I thought, right, I have to do something about this."

‌



Fortunately, TfL's then-operations and asset maintenance director Nigel Holness managed to arrange for Margaret to be given a CD containing her late husband's voice, and his announcement remains audible today on the northbound Northern Line platform at Embankment.

Viewers responding to Russ' video were touched by the tale. One commented: "As a regular user of Embankment Tube Station, I had not noticed this until you pointed it out. It is different elsewhere. How sweet! I love TFL."

Another remarked: "That voice was there for decades. I remember it from when I used to get the tube into London from Watford aged 14 (1988 onwards)."

Article continues below

While someone else posted: "I thought it sounded familiar. I haven't been a regular on the tube since 1985. I just did a little digging and he was the voice of the tube throughout the 70s and 80s, which is why it felt so natural to me."

News.title: Trump cancels Catholic charity contract worth millions after feud with Pope Leo
News.content:
Trump cancels Catholic charity contract worth millions after feud with Pope Leo

Catholic charity leader Thomas Wenski said the move would destroy the Florida charity, which provides critical help for unaccompanied children, within three months

View 4 Images Trump has rescinded critical funding for a Catholic charity (Image: Andrew Leyden/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump has turned up the heat on his feud with Pope Leo in a bizarre move targeting the Catholic Church's support for migrants.

‌



The US president, who this week in an extraordinary broadside slammed the Vatican chief as "weak on crime" and "even worse on foreign policy", has rescinded federal funding for a charity that aids migrants. The Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Miami, in Florida, has for the last 60 years provided housing and assistance to migrant children, aided by $11 million (£8.1 million) in funding from the federal government.

‌



Without that, it has been warned, the charity could be forced to close in a year, with the archbishop of Miami branding the decision "baffling".

‌



View 4 Images Trump has been repeatedly disparaging of the first American Pope (Image: Andrew Leyden/ZUMA Press Wire/REX/Shutterstock)

The Daily Beast reports that the funding was withdrawn by the Department of Health and Human services as the number of children under the care of the archdiocese had decreased. It claimed the number of beneficiaries has dropped down to 1,900 under Donald Trump from 22,000 under his predecessor Joe Biden.

The move, it added, was first discussed in March, a month before the president started feuding with the first American Pope, whose real name is Robert Francis Provost. Archbishop of Miami Thomas Wenski predicted that, without the vital funding, the more than half-a-century-old organisation would last just another three months.

‌



He announced the cancellation of funding on the archdiocese website, saying the crucial support for unaccompanied children would be lost. He said: "For more than 60 years, the Archdiocese of Miami’s services for unaccompanied minors have been recognized for their excellence and have served as a model for other agencies throughout the country.

View 4 Images Thomas Wenski said the charity wouldn't last three months without federal funding (Image: Pedro Portal/TNS via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"Our track record in serving this vulnerable population is unmatched. Yet, the Archdiocese of Miami’s Catholic Charities’ services for unaccompanied minors has been stripped of funding and will be forced to shut down within three months." He said it was "baffling" the government would choose to shut down a programme with so many proven benefits.

‌



He added: "But given the history and reputation of the Msgr Bryan O Walsh Children’s Village it is baffling that the US government would shut down a program that it would be hard-pressed to replicate at the level of competence and excellence that Catholic Charities has achieved if and when future waves of unaccompanied minors reach our shores."

View 4 Images Pope Leo appeared to hit back at Trump during his Africa tour (Image: VATICAN MEDIA HANDOUT/EPA/Shutterstock)

While not explicitly linked to Trump's war of words with the Pope, the shutdown comes at a time of heightened tensions between the two figures.

Article continues below

The Pope himself, who has previously said he isn't afraid of the Trump administration, appeared to turn up the temperature with Trump earlier this week when he warned the world was "being wage by a handful of tyrants" who spend billions on wars. The outspoken Pontiff criticised leaders who use "the very name of God" to launch conflict while stopping in Cameroon during his tour of Africa.

News.title: Police review case of Lee Boxell who vanished 38 years ago 'after defying paedo'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Police review case of Lee Boxell who vanished 38 years ago 'after defying paedo'

Lee Boxell's disappearance is being re-examined by the Met Police Cold Case Unit, offering his family a "last chance" for answers nearly 40 years after the teen vanished in 1988

View 8 Images Lee Boxell was 15 at the time of his disappearance (Image: PA)

Nearly four decades after 15-year-old Lee Boxell vanished without a trace, the bedroom in his family home remains frozen in time - and his parents refuse to change their number in case he calls.

Now, in what his 79-year-old father Peter calls a "last chance" for the truth, the Metropolitan Police has officially reopened the investigation into one of UK's most haunting cold cases.

The dedicated Cold Case Review Team is set to pore over a "room full of documents" to finally uncover what happened to the football-mad teenager who disappeared in 1988.

The fresh probe will apply modern forensic techniques to old evidence - including a watch found years ago - as investigators revisit a sinister network of grooming and abuse linked to an outbuilding at a local church.

Half-siblings' secret relationship uncovered after police order DNA test for child READ MORE :

View 8 Images Lee's parents Peter and Christine have never given up hope (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Lee's father, Peter Boxell, now 79, said the fresh probe offers a final opportunity for answers after years of heartbreak and uncertainty. "It's a last chance to find out what happened to Lee," he tells the Mirror. "The Cold Case Review Team will be going through everything that the police has on the files, which is a whole room of documents to check everything was done properly.

"It's a last chance for us to find out. I'm just hopeful." Lee, from Sutton, South London, was last seen on September 10, 1988, after telling his family he was heading to a football match. He never returned home.

Despite a major police investigation, no one has ever been charged. Former detective Mark Williams-Thomas, who has conducted his own investigation into the case, revealed the review has just started after officials approached the family.

"They approached the family about a month ago and they pulled all the paperwork together because over the years, it's ended up at different stations," he tells the Mirror.

"I'm really pleased because it needs a focus on it." Mark has worked closely with the Boxell family while producing his podcast episode The Detective: Lee Boxell, in which he examined evidence and interviewed key witnesses.

View 8 Images A campaign was launched to find Lee but the case went cold (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

"We did a big investigation and we uncovered a network of paedophilia in the area at the time of Lee's disappearance," he said. "I'll be waiting for a call from the police because I'll share more recent information from people who didn't speak out at the time."

For Lee's family, the pain has endured for nearly 40 years. "We've never given up hope, we're getting old and the hope of finding an answer is diminishing," Peter said.

"This is our last opportunity to find out what happened to Lee. His sister needs to know, and now he has a nephew and a niece but they all know about him."

The family home remains filled with reminders of the missing teenager. Mark explains that the family have kept his room almost perfectly intact, while they refuse to change their home phone number or address in the hopes Lee might return.

View 8 Images Lee had been attending an unofficial youth club (Image: Collect)

"They still have memories at home," Mark adds. "They've never moved address for desire for Lee to come back, never changed their telephone number because he knows it, but they are realistic that he is likely dead."

They have also drawn strength from support networks over the years. "We need an answer, but we're lucky we've had support from the Missing People charity, and also from friends at the choir who we meet once a month."

Helen Alves, Head of Support Services at Missing People charity, tells the Mirror: "We welcome the news that the Cold Case Unit has reopened the investigation into the disappearance of Lee Boxell. Any renewed focus on Lee's case is an important step towards finding answers, and we fully support further inquests or lines of enquiry that may help bring clarity to what happened.

"As a charity, we know that for families of missing people, the passage of time does not lessen the need for answers. No matter how long someone has been missing, the uncertainty remains, and families deserve resolution.

"Our thoughts are with Lee's family and friends at this time. We will continue to be here to support them for as long as they need us. We also stand behind the police in their efforts and hope that this renewed investigation brings meaningful progress."

‌



View 8 Images Lee's parents also want answers for his sister (Image: COPYRIGHT, 2010)

From the outset, the case was marked by disturbing claims and unanswered questions. One of the last reported sightings of Lee was on Sutton High Street, South London.

The football mad youngster, who would have turned 53 this year, had £10 in his pocket and was first thought to be on his way to watch Crystal Palace at nearby Selhurst Park.

‌



But detectives discovered in 2012 that he would spend time in an outbuilding of St Dunstan's church at Cheam village, known to regulars as the Shed.

Allegations emerged of abuse, grooming and a network of offenders operating in the area during the late 1980s and early 1990s. Some claimed Lee had been killed and buried in the church grounds, while others said he was living under a new identity.

In 2013, Crimewatch featured another appeal for information, which led to an allegation of sexual abuse never reported. Police began working on the theory that "Lee may have died after intervening to try to stop sexual abuse at a youth club in Cheam".

‌



View 8 Images Lee's childhood bedroom has remained intact (Image: COPYRIGHT, 2011)

Despite a steady flow of intelligence, no definitive breakthrough was made. Peter believes the difference now lies in the team handling the case.

"It has been reviewed a few times by the detectives that were working on the case, but they can't devote all of their time to it because they work on live cases," he said.

‌



"The team are different, they will see it through from beginning to end. I’m hopeful we will get some answers."

He also reflected on a major excavation more than a decade ago. "Some arrests were made a few years ago, but this was when the police excavated an entire graveyard and they arrested William Lambert.

"They didn't manage to find any forensic evidence to link Lee's possible murder with Lambert."

‌



Steve Lambert, the son of convicted paedophile gravedigger William, believes his father murdered Lee. Lambert, who was 85 at the time of his arrest, was taken into custody on ­suspicion of Lee's murder but later released without charge.

Lambert ran the club that Lee attended and was later convicted of encouraging youngsters to engage in sexual activity by pretending he had supernatural powers.

View 8 Images Lee and Christine, both in their 70s, believe this is their 'final chance' at answers

‌



He was jailed for 11 years in 2011 for sexually abusing four girls in the grounds of St Dunstan’s Church between 1985 and 1987. He was convicted of rape, indecent assault and procuring girls to have sex by false pretences. Three years later, Lambert was held over Lee's murder along with nephew Robert Smith and a third man.

Mark previously told us that he believed Lambert was the man behind Lee's disappearance. "I believe that on the day Lee disappeared he witnessed something and Lambert could not trust him to keep quiet so he was silenced, killed by Lambert," he said.

In a four-part podcast, he asked his son Steve if he thought his dad was capable of murdering a child. He replied: "I think so, if he got caught out. I believe if he got caught out and he believed there was a risk of ­somebody telling the police. He got away with it, you could say he got away with murder."

‌



View 8 Images William Lambert was convicted of sexual abuse (Image: PA)

While the review brings renewed hope, investigators are not working with fresh evidence - at least for now. "There's no direct new evidence," Mark said.

"The cold case review team look to apply modern techniques to old evidence." He pointed to key material that could still yield answers. "We know there is some evidence, a watch that was found that I want them to do more forensics [on].

‌



"There's quite a lot of paperwork to review, a lot of witnesses to speak to, and we uncovered new information that hadn't been in the public domain previously."

For the Boxell family, the stakes could not be higher. "We are very pleased that [the Cold Case Unit] have taken this on," Peter said. "It's our last chance."

As detectives begin the painstaking process of re-examining decades of evidence, the hope is that advances in forensic science and a fresh perspective may finally succeed where previous investigations fell short.

News.title: XL bully owner jailed after 'confused' pensioner mauled to death and 'eaten'
News.content:
XL bully owner jailed after 'confused' pensioner mauled to death and 'eaten'

Sean Garner, 31, has been jailed at Liverpool Crown Court for being the owner of an XL bully dog which killed 84-year-old John McColl in a “savage attack”

View Image Sean Garner, the owner of an XL bully which savaged a pensioner (Image: PA)

An XL bully breeder has been jailed for 12 years after his dog mauled a pensioner to death.

‌



Sean Garner, 31, has been jailed at Liverpool Crown Court for being the owner of an XL bully dog which killed 84-year-old John McColl in a “savage attack” in Warrington, Cheshire, in February last year.

‌



Mr McColl, 84, was attacked by the dog after he wandered onto the driveway of Garner's home and died from his injuries about a month later. The animal, which was called Toretto and weighed seven stone and four pounds, was shot 10 times by armed police.

‌



Garner, was found guilty at Liverpool Crown Court last month of being the owner of a dog which caused injury while dangerously out of control.

The jury heard Mr McColl was on his way home from the pub shortly after 6pm on February 24 when he walked into the driveway of Garner’s home, where the dog had been left on a patio area which the prosecution alleged was only secured by a gate with a latch.

News.title: 'I pulled my kids out of the "bonkers school system" after my son's sad admission'
News.content:
'I pulled my kids out of the "bonkers school system" after my son's sad admission'

Lisa Percival took her children; Hunter and Pandora out of school last year to spend six months "world schooling" them, where traditional education is replaced with travel and experiential learning

View 4 Images Lisa Percival, pictured with her family, spoke about the way she educates her kids (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

A mum has pulled her children out of Britain’s “bonkers” school system to take them on trips around the world after her son said he would “rather die” than attend.

‌



Lisa Percival, 37, took her children, Hunter, 10, and Pandora, eight, out of school last year to spend six months “world schooling” them, where traditional education is replaced with immersive travel and experiential learning. The mum insists she was “forced” to pull her son, who suffers from emotionally-based school avoidance (EBSA), from school in April 2025 after he said he’d rather die than attend.

‌



Emotionally-based school avoidance is a term for children experiencing severe anxiety that prevents them from attending school. Often, sufferers will get physical symptoms, including stomach pain and headaches.

‌



View 4 Images Lisa Percival's children; Pandora and Hunter, are pictured on a holiday (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

Struggling to get her son to school, Lisa came up with her plan to “world school” him. World schooling is an educational approach where families travel and use “the world as a classroom”. Children learn from real-world experiences and are taught by their parents rather than learning in a classroom.

Lisa, who lives in Kettering, Northamptonshire, said: “It wasn’t my decision, and I was totally forced into it. When things were going wrong at school, Hunter was having meltdowns every single hour, and he was so depressed.

‌



“This wasn’t a kid just saying ‘I don’t want to go to school because I want to play on my Xbox today’, he couldn’t get out of bed. The schools were saying, ‘if you don’t get him in, you could get fined, and if you don’t get him in, this could be referred to social services as neglect’.”

In October 2023, Lisa was hit with a £60 fine per child for taking her children on holiday to Cyprus during term time, which pushed her to permanently remove them from school.

She then discovered a World Schooling Facebook page – and decided to travel the world with her kids instead. The family then visited school hubs – temporary, mobile, week-long gatherings designed to bring worldschoolers together — in Portugal, South Goa, and Bulgaria.

‌



The landlord says she is grateful to be able to balance her job with worldschooling, which puts less pressure on her kids. Lisa also believes British schools are “ridiculous” for issuing fines for taking kids out of school in term time, which she believes puts a “tax on family time”.

View 4 Images Lisa Percival has taken kids Hunter, 10, and Pandora, 8, out of school (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

Taking to Instagram, the mother shared footage from their trip to India and said: “Day in the life of a home educating parent”. In the clip, you can see Hunter beaming at the camera during a dolphin boat trip with the World School Hub, while another shows Pandora taking part in an aerial skills class.

‌



After returning home for a reset in February 2026, Lisa says she educates her kids at home and insists they are both “much happier now” than they were in school.

She now vows to never send her kids to mainstream school again and plans to continue travelling to different world school hubs in the future.

She adds: “We didn’t know how bad things were until Hunter said he’d rather die than go to school. That was the turning point. I was like ‘we really need to do something now’.”

‌



She says they noticed several issues with the school system: “I think it’s possibly a combination of unmet needs at school and a terrible environment. My son was put in a classroom that didn’t even have a window. It was too noisy for him, and he couldn’t get away from it. The curriculum is also a huge problem. The kids today are not interested in it.”

She believes interactive, immersive and experiential learning is the best way — and thinks some lessons should be optional. After deregistering both her kids from school last year, the family visited various world school hubs during their travels, including a four-week programme in Portugal.

Lisa says the full-time programme included day trips and learning about AI, and her son had a tutor twice a week to keep up with the UK curriculum.

‌



Her trips also included six weeks in Bulgaria and more than two months in India. Lisa says: “Worldschooling has opened our eyes to new experiences and new ways of living. What we liked about it was how the rest of the community had the same sort of mindset as us. It was a different way of life.

“It was much less academic and less pressure, and more education was focused on the actual child and how they were socially and emotionally. A lot of the curriculum is skill-based.”

“That’s the problem with British schools is that’s all they care about. They don’t really care about the children. Our kids are way ahead, and we push them far too early.”

‌



View 4 Images Lisa Percival has taken kids Hunter, 10, and Pandora, 8, out of school (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

She also says starting school at age four is “ridiculous”. “It’s so damaging for their wellbeing. What’s absolutely bonkers is that people like me can deregister and do what the hell we want.

“If I asked my child’s school if I could go to India for a month, they’d have said ‘no’, so instead I’ve deregistered my daughter, and she’s now been out of school for five months. It doesn’t make sense at all.

‌



“I feel grateful that I can balance my job and give my kids the home-schooling opportunity. I feel super lucky. But it wasn’t easy, and I made sacrifices.”

After returning to the UK, Lisa now homeschools her kids, and they attend daily social groups so they still get to meet friends. She hopes to spread awareness about the difference between home schooling, where a child remains enrolled at a school and follows the curriculum and elective home education where the parent takes full responsibility for their child’s education outside of a school setting.

Lisa says: “I’ve noticed a change in [my kids] and especially in Hunter. Now, he wakes up happily and can make his own breakfast, and cook for himself during the day, and he can do basic levels of work.

‌



“He’s so much happier now, and I think that’s down to us taking the pressure and demands off him, and taking him out of school has really helped.”

She wants to squash the negative opinions around home schooling too. Lisa says: “People in the UK don’t like the term home schooling. It’s important to spread awareness about the difference. A lot of people get confused. Nothing we do is like school at all. We’re educating them and not schooling them.”

She added: “Even though things are starting to change as people are realising the school system is c**p, there’s not enough out there. I’d never send my kids back to mainstream school.”

Article continues below

Now the mum encourages other parents to consider home educating if their child is unhappy at school: “I would encourage parents to be open-minded and research home education in their area if school is not working for them.

“School works well for lots of parents, and that’s fine, and their choice, but before they demonise home education or home schooling, what I’d say is start researching.”

News.title: Met Office names areas Brits are braced for SNOW — full list of blizzard locations
News.content:
Met Office names areas Brits are braced for SNOW — full list of blizzard locations

UK weather maps show snow could hit parts of the UK in the final days of April, with Scotland, northern England and even Birmingham set to be affected by blizzards and icy conditions

View 2 Images (Image: PA)

Some parts of the UK could experience snow towards the month's end as the prolonged spell of unsettled weather persists, forecasters understand.

‌



A long-range forecast from the Met Office indicated that while sunny intervals might reach the country initially, northerly winds delivering wintry showers to northern and eastern coastlines, and some snow could subsequently return, particularly in northern Scotland.

‌



The forecast, spanning Tuesday, April 21 to Thursday, April 30, stated: "High pressure to the north of the UK will bring plenty of dry weather and sunny spells at first. A few scattered showers are possible in central and eastern areas.

‌



"Parts of the east coast could be on the chilly side with low cloud and an onshore breeze, but further west it will feel quite warm, especially in sunnier areas. By the weekend, unsettled weather is signalled to return, but confidence in the details is low with a range of scenarios possible. One scenario is for a northerly wind bringing wintry showers to northern and eastern coasts, and some snow over Scottish mountains. If this does occur it will probably not last more than a few days, before high pressure attempts to return towards the end of the month."

Kill weeds instantly with 39p cupboard staple – it also deters pests READ MORE :

View 2 Images April is expected to become cold (Image: PA)

‌



Other regions of the UK, meanwhile, could be affected by snow during the same timeframe. Maps from WXCharts.com suggest a cold snap that might bring frigid temperatures and snow to areas of the UK on Saturday, April 25. The chilliest regions will be across the north of the UK, encompassing Scotland and northern England. Certain parts of Scotland, particularly around Aberdeen, could witness as much as 6cm of snow. Blizzards, though, could also strike as far south as Birmingham, the same charts indicate, reports the Express.

Additional areas expected to be affected include the north west of England, particularly around Blackpool and Manchester, which could see 3cm of snow coverage.

April's weather has been erratic so far, featuring a succession of mini heatwaves and cold spells. These snow blizzards will be succeeded by a 23C scorcher on Wednesday, April 29, the latest forecast suggests.

Article continues below

A Met Office forecast spanning April 21 to April 30 stated: "High pressure to the north of the UK will bring plenty of dry weather and sunny spells at first. A few scattered showers are possible in central and eastern areas.

"Parts of the east coast could be on the chilly side with low cloud and an onshore breeze, but further west it will feel quite warm, especially in sunnier areas. By the weekend, unsettled weather is signalled to return, but confidence in the details is low with a range of scenarios possible.

"One scenario is for a northerly wind bringing wintry showers to northern and eastern coasts, and some snow over Scottish mountains. If this does occur, it will probably not last more than a few days before high pressure attempts to return towards the end of the month."

News.title: Home Bargains £10 lamp makes rooms look 'elegant' and rivals £41 Homebase version
News.content:
Home Bargains £10 lamp makes rooms look 'elegant' and rivals £41 Homebase version

Home Bargains is selling an 'exquisite' ceramic table lamp for spring that shoppers say could brighten up your living space on a budget

View 3 Images "Elevate your living space with this exquisite ceramic table lamp" (Image: Getty )

Home Bargains is stocking a lamp hailed as 'exquisite', which could serve as a wallet-friendly alternative to a similar design available elsewhere on the high street. With spring now in full swing, many households will be refreshing their interiors, including revamping their living areas.

‌



One possibility for those looking to 'elevate' their home without breaking the bank can be found at Home Bargains as part of its newest homeware collection. The retailer is offering an Esme Ceramic Lamp, which could compete with a comparable version sold at Homebase, reports the Liverpool Echo.

‌



The discount retailer's lamp is priced at £9.99 and boasts a ripple-effect base alongside a cream-coloured shade. It needs an E14 Max. 40W bulb, and is intended to introduce 'timeless elegance' to whichever room it's placed in.

‌



On the Home Bargains website, the product description states: "Brighten up your home with the Home Collections Ceramic Lamp - Esme! This stunning handcrafted lamp combines contemporary style with timeless elegance, making it the perfect accent for any decor."

It added: "Elevate your living space with this exquisite ceramic table lamp, blending contemporary design with timeless craftsmanship. This lamp stands as a testament to the beauty of handcrafted ceramics, featuring a sleek silhouette that complements modern and traditional decor alike."

View 3 Images Home Bargains' Esme Ceramic Lamp is £9.99 (Image: Home Bargains)

‌



At first glance, the £9.99 lamp could be mistaken for Homebase's Acacia Home Fabric Shade Pot Table Lamp. Both designs showcase a 'ripple-effect' base and a light-coloured shade. The Homebase alternative, however, carries a £31 premium, priced at £41.

Though on further examination, several distinctions exist between the two beyond cost, including neck colour, shape, and size. But the Home Bargains lamp might be an economical choice for those seeking a comparable aesthetic without the expense.

Homebase's product listing for its £41 Acacia Home Fabric Shade Pot Table Lamp states: "Introduce a welcoming ambience to any room with this classically designed table lamp. Boasting a timeless base and a quality fabric shade, it effortlessly enhances both contemporary and traditional décor.

‌



View 3 Images Homebase's £41 Acacia Home Fabric Shade Pot Table Lamp (Image: Homebase)

"For ease of use, it includes a convenient inline rocker switch, and the double insulation offers added safety. Ideal for adding warm light and creating a cosy atmosphere on your bedside table or in your living room, this lamp combines functionality with undeniable charm."

Meanwhile, at Home Bargains, the retailer is also stocking a trio of U-Shaped Oak Shelves for £4.99. The "easy to wall-mount" shelving units are described as a "perfect" method to showcase your treasured ornaments and provide storage across three tiers.

Article continues below

The Home Bargains shelving is presently amongst the most affordable sets available. B&Q is retailing a comparable option for £26, the Set of Three U-Shaped Floating Wooden Shelf, though these feature a considerably darker finish.

News.title: Why the UK is preparing for food shortages due to Iran war

The UK could face food shortages by the summer if the Iran war continues, a worst case scenario drawn up by government officials suggests.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz could continue to disrupt global supply chains, leading to shortages of carbon dioxide (CO2), which is used in the food and drinks industry.

A spokesperson from the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs said these scenarios are planning tools, not predictions of future events.

News.title: Watch: Reporter told to fake domestic abuse claim to remain in the UK
News.content:
Migrants are falsely claiming to be victims of domestic abuse in order to stay in the country, exploiting rules brought in to expedite the process of securing permanent residence for genuine abuse victims

A BBC investigation has found that legal advisers are encouraging some to make up abuse allegations. One of those advisers, Eli Ciswaka, encouraged a BBC reporter to make false allegations of domestic abuse - saying that he would fabricate the claim for £900, creating a story to tell the Home Office in order to secure the client's status in the UK.

Ciswaka did not respond to a written request for comment, but during a phone call to tell him about our investigation he denied being willing to make up a story that the undercover reporter had been a victim of domestic abuse.

Jess Phillips, the minister for safeguarding in the Home Office, said that the abuse of rules around domestic abuse victims was "unacceptable" and that "sham lawyers facilitating this advice abuse will be put behind bars."

Two men were disqualified from one of South Africa's flagship marathon races after they finished in the top 10 of the women's race in an example of cheating that has overshadowed the performance of honest runners.

Their attempt at swapping bibs, which bear the identification numbers worn by racers, resulted in two women runners initially finishing outside the top 10 in the Two Oceans Marathon in Cape Town on April 12.

The annual Two Oceans race is one of South Africa’s iconic marathons and includes a 56-kilometer (34.7-mile) ultramarathon and a 21.1-kilometer (13.1-mile) half-marathon. The event attracts over 16,000 participants and finishing among the top 10 is a significant achievement for most runners.

The two men, Luke Jacobs and Nic Bradfield, finished seventh and 10th. They were disqualified after a marathon board member uncovered the deception. The women runners who had been bumped were subsequently recognized for their legitimate finishes.

Jacobs and Bradfield will face disciplinary processes by the marathon’s disciplinary subcommittee, said Two Oceans Marathon board member Stuart Mann, who helped uncover the deception.

Swapping bibs is unethical and risky

Exchanging bibs with another marathoner has become more common while also carrying far-reaching consequences, Mann said.

“Not only is it considered unethical, but it also poses health and medicals risks in case of an emergency as wrong medication may be administered to a wrong person,” Mann said.

Swapping numbers can result from different motivations, Mann explained. For some, it is done to avoid losing money if they are injured or for some other unexpected reason can’t run the race. For others, the deceptive practice allows them to obtain a faster time to use for qualifying in a future race.

Online photos lead to discoveries and apologies

Mann was tipped off to one of the swaps after Jacobs posted pictures of himself at the race on social media and people noticed his bib displayed the name “Larissa.”

After further investigation, Mann learned Jacobs competed using a bib assigned to Larissa Parekh, who was registered to compete in the women's race.

“I made an error in judgment and did not consider the consequences. I should not have taken part,” Jacobs said in a written apology.

James and Bradfield also were tripped up by modern sports technology. Race officials watched the first 10 women cross the finish line, but data from chips in the bibs indicated two other women also had crossed, although they were not observed by the officials.

The discrepancy led to the revelation that Bradfield competed with a number belonging to Tegan Garvey, who later admitted to giving up her bib after she suffered a hip problem prior to the race.

“The day before, my hip gave in completely, leaving me unable to even walk. I felt bad as to give up my race entry so my friend ran in my place,” Garvey said.

Parekh did not give a clear explanation for her actions, according to Mann, who said both women have apologized and face two-year bans from the Two Oceans Marathon.

Around 15 people deported from the United States landed in Congo’s capital Kinshasa in the early hours of Friday, one of their lawyers told The Associated Press.

It was the latest example of the Trump administration using agreements with African countries to accelerate migrant removals under controversial circumstances that have raised questions about respect for the migrants' rights.

An official at the Congolese migration agency confirmed the arrivals but didn’t provide details.

The deportees are all from Latin America and the Congolese government plans to keep them in the country for a short period, said U.S. attorney Alma David, who represents one of the deportees and has been speaking with her client since arriving in Kinshasa.

All the deportees are believed to have legal protection from U.S. judges shielding them against being returned to their home countries, David said. The deportees are believed to be staying at a hotel in Kinshasa.

The International Organization for Migration, a United Nations-affiliated agency, will be involved to offer “assisted voluntary return,” David told AP.

“The fact that the focus is on offering them ‘voluntary’ return to their home country when they spent months in immigration detention in the U.S. fighting hard to not have to go home is very alarming,” she said.

The IOM didn't immediately respond to AP's request for comment.

Congo's Ministry of Communications said in a statement earlier this month that it will receive some migrants as part of a new deal under the Trump administration’s third-country program.

It described the arrangement as a “temporary” one that reflects Congo’s “commitment to human dignity and international solidarity.” It would come with zero costs to the government with the U.S. covering the needed logistics, it said.

The statement said no automatic transfer of the deportees is planned, adding: “Each situation will be subject to individual review in accordance with the laws of the Republic and national security requirements.”

The U.S. has struck such third-country deportation deals with at least seven other African nations, many of them among countries hit the most by the Trump administration’s policies that have restricted trade, aid and migration.

The Trump administration has spent at least $40 million to deport about 300 migrants to countries other than their own, according to a report released recently by the Democratic staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

Lawyers and activists have raised questions over the nature of the deals with countries in Africa and elsewhere. Several of the African nations that have signed such deals have notoriously repressive governments and poor human rights records — including Eswatini, South Sudan and Equatorial Guinea.

——

This story has been corrected to show that Alma David is one of several lawyers representing the deportees.

——

Banchereau reported from Dakar, Senegal. Associated Press writer Saleh Mwanamilongo in Bonn, Germany contributed to this report.

News.title: Scammers used AI images to try and swindle $2,800 from desperate family searching for missing dog
News.content:

A Florida family says scammers tried to swindle them out of nearly $2,800 by using AI-generated images to make it appear their missing dog was injured and in need of emergency surgery.

The ordeal began Saturday night in Deltona, when Bill Cosens said the family’s Beagle mix, Archer, escaped from the backyard, he told Fox 35 Orlando. The family posted a photo of their beloved pet on Facebook, asking for the community’s help in bringing him home.

By Sunday morning, the family received a call from someone claiming the dog had been hit by a car and urgently needed surgery. The caller demanded nearly $2,800 upfront and sent what appeared to be convincing proof: photos of Archer on an operating table in a veterinary clinic.

However, a closer look at the photos revealed troubling inconsistencies, including irregularities in the dog’s fur and an X-ray in the images dated 2022.

“This isn’t Archer. This is AI,” Cosens said, recalling the moment the deception became clear. “It wasn’t obvious when you’re distraught.”

open image in gallery This is one of the AI-generated images the Cosens family received from scammers, who demanded nearly $2,800 while falsely claiming their dog, Archer, had been hit by a car and needed emergency surgery ( AI/The Cosens Family )

open image in gallery The family noticed inconsistencies in the AI dog's fur, as well as the pictured X-ray, dated 2022 ( AI )

The final red flag was that the address provided for the supposed "veterinary clinic" was really Deltona City Hall. Now knowing that it was all a ruse, Cosens turned to his neighbor for help. The man claimed he had seen a woman pick up Archer and drive away with him on the night he disappeared.

"He’s like, ‘Man, people are so low," Cosens recalled the conversation with his neighbor. "He says, ‘Do me a favor. Send me the information, the texts, the pictures and the telephone number. I got ways I can track people.’"

The neighbor ultimately tracked the woman down to a nearby location, and Archer was returned home safe Thursday morning, Cosens told WESH, adding that the animal is “physically, emotionally, mentally just worn out.”

This scam is believed to be part of a growing trend in which criminals monitor social media, especially “lost pet” posts, to find vulnerable owners. They can take real photos shared online and use AI to create fake, emotionally charged situations, like injuries or emergency vet visits, to pressure people into paying quickly.

Reflecting on the ordeal, Cosens said he’s grateful for his neighbor’s help in safely bringing Archer back home, ending what could have been both an emotional and financial loss.

"I have to remind myself, as much as I’ve lost faith in humanity as a whole, then I look at my neighbor and go without him, I wouldn’t have my dog back," Cosens told Fox 35 Orlando.

The Volusia County Sheriff’s Office is investigating this case.

The Independent has contacted the sheriff’s office for comment.

News.content:

Police officers have arrested a woman after a seven-year-old autistic girl was found dead in a golf course pond.

Nyla May Bradshaw was found unresponsive in a pond on Owston Golf Course, north of Doncaster, South Yorkshire, on 30 March.

South Yorkshire Police said on Friday that a woman aged in her 30s has been arrested on suspicion of gross negligence manslaughter and child neglect.

She has been bailed pending further inquiries, the force said.

Detective Chief Inspector Gary Magnay said while initial inquiries had indicated the circumstances of Nyla’s death were not suspicious, police had “furthered (their) investigation into the events leading up to the incident”.

An inquest opening earlier this month heard Nyla was “a non-verbal seven-year-old girl who had been diagnosed with autism”.

Coroner’s officer Jane McDonnell said Nyla was being looked after by a childminder and “during the course of the day she was taken out to a park in the Owston area of Doncaster”.

open image in gallery South Yorkshire Police said on Friday that a woman aged in her 30s has been arrested on suspicion of gross negligence manslaughter and child neglect ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

She said: “During the course of the excursion she passed through a gap in the fence and approached woodland close to Owston Golf Course.”

Ms McDonnell said a search began after the childminder raised the alarm with police and Nyla’s family.

The girl was found unresponsive and face down in a pond on the golf course, the officer told Doncaster’s senior coroner Nicola Mundy.

Nyla was taken to hospital but could not be resuscitated, the court heard.

Mr Magnay said: “The heart-breaking loss of Nyla May has had a huge emotional impact – not just on her family, friends and loved ones, but on the wider community.

“Nyla May’s family continues to be in the forefront of our thoughts as our work progresses, and we will continue to support them throughout this awful time.

“Since this tragedy, our officers have been working hard to establish the full circumstances surrounding Nyla’s death.

“While initial inquiries indicated the circumstances were not suspicious, these ongoing inquiries have ultimately led us to make this arrest and further our investigation in relation to the events leading up to the incident.

“The proceedings in this case are now active, which means nothing must be published by anyone, including members of the public, which could threaten the integrity of any future court proceedings.

“For this reason, I’d urge the public to not speculate about the incident, including on social media, and respect the privacy of all those affected.”
